# LPG traders call off strike after BERC promises to hear demands

## Traders seek Tk 150 per cylinder, fair transport charges and an end to fines "harassment"

 

 bdnews24.com News Service 

 Published : 14 Oct 2026, 05:52 PM 

 Updated : 14 Oct 2026, 05:52 PM 

LPG traders have withdrawn their planned two-day shutdown after securing talks with the energy regulator over seven demands, including higher commissions and an end to alleged harassment.

The LP Gas Traders Cooperative Association scrapped the plan on Wednesday after talks with the chairman of the Bangladesh Energy Regulatory Commission (BERC).

Association President Md Selim Khan told bdnews24.com the BERC chairman assured them at a 3pm meeting that their demands would be heard at a public hearing on Oct 29.

âIn light of this, we are withdrawing the strike,â he said.

The association had earlier announced that all LPG shops across the country would remain closed on Oct 15 and 16.

At Mondayâs press conference at the National Press Club, Selim warned that traders would close their shops indefinitely if their demands were not met within two days.

Earlier on Wednesday, Power Minister Iqbal Hassan Mahmood Tuku and Commerce Minister Khandaker Abdul Muktadir held a meeting with LPG importers and operators.

At a press conference after the meeting, the power minister warned that legal action would be taken against the traders concerned unless they withdrew the strike.

âIf they do not withdraw the strike, the government will take legal action,â he said.

He said LPG is an essential commodity and attempts to press demands by disrupting its supply were unacceptable. He said action could be taken under the Essential Commodities Control Act of 1956.

At the same briefing, the commerce minister said businesses could have concerns over commissions, profits and losses or other issues, but such problems must be resolved through discussions.

He said the relevant authorities were ready to hear the traders' grievances.

However, he warned that businesses would not be allowed to exploit the market situation for their own interests.

âThe government will not tolerate any attempt to use this as a pretext to hold the country hostage,â the commerce minister said.

After the ministersâ warnings, the association met the BERC chairman and scrapped the shutdown plan.

The association's key demand is that distributors' commission on each LPG cylinder be raised to Tk 150 or set at 7 percent of the retail price.

At Monday's press conference, Selim said BERC had set the distributors' commission at Tk 50 per cylinder five years ago.

Since then, costs for fuel, transportation, loading and unloading cylinders, warehouse rent and licences have all increased.

In a letter to BERC, the association said it costs Tk 50 to transport a cylinder from a company to a distributor's warehouse.

Published: 2026-10-14
Author: UNB

UNB 14 October, 2026, 06:25 pm Last modified: 14 October, 2026, 08:07 pm 

## Their demands include an end to alleged administrative harassment, a review of operatorsâ commission rates and the release of thousands of unused gas cylinders into the domestic supply chain. 

 UNB 14 October, 2026, 06:25 pm Last modified: 14 October, 2026, 08:07 pm 

 Representational image. Photo: TBS 

Liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) traders have called off their planned two-day nationwide strike scheduled for Thursday and Friday (15â16 October ).

Selim Khan, president of the LPG Traders Cooperative Association, announced the decision on Wednesday following a high-level meeting at the Secretariat and the scheduling of a public hearing on LPG pricing for 29 October.

Earlier, Power, Energy and Mineral Resources Minister Iqbal Hassan Mahmood Tuku and Commerce Minister Khandaker Abdul Muktadir warned of stern legal action against traders if they proceeded with the planned nationwide suspension of LPG cylinder sales and distribution.

The warning came after the LPG distributors' platform announced on Monday (12 October ) a complete shutdown of LPG outlets across the country on 15 and 16 October to press home several demands.

Their demands include an end to alleged administrative harassment, a review of operators' commission rates and the release of thousands of unused gas cylinders into the domestic supply chain.

With the strike called off, traders are expected to raise their demands and pricing concerns at the public hearing scheduled for 29 October.

# 12kg LPG cylinder price rises by Tk252 to Tk1,837 | The Business Standard
URL: https://www.tbsnews.net/economy/energy/12kg-lpg-cylinder-price-rises-tk252-tk1837-1562271
Published: 2026-10-04
Author: TBS Report

TBS Report 04 October, 2026, 05:30 pm Last modified: 04 October, 2026, 07:23 pm 

## The Bangladesh Energy Regulatory Commission (BERC) announced the new price today, with the revised rate taking effect from 6pm. 

 TBS Report 04 October, 2026, 05:30 pm Last modified: 04 October, 2026, 07:23 pm 

 Representational image. Photo: TBS 

The price of a 12kg liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) cylinder has been increased by Tk252, taking the price to Tk1,837.

The Bangladesh Energy Regulatory Commission (BERC) announced the new price today (4 October), with the revised rate taking effect from 6pm.

In September, BERC had reduced the price of a 12kg LPG cylinder by Tk13 to Tk1,585.

According to a BERC press notification issued today, the regulator calculated the October price based on Saudi Aramco's Contract Price (CP) for propane and butane, which stood at $680 and $730 per tonne respectively.

The average Saudi CP was therefore set at $712.50 per tonne. The commission also considered $250 per tonne in shipping and trader premiums and an average exchange rate of Tk123.18 per US dollar while determining the new price.

The price of private LPG at the retail level has been set at Tk153.06 per kg, including VAT. Accordingly, the price of a 12kg LPG cylinder has been fixed at Tk1,837, including VAT.

The BERC has also revised the prices of LPG cylinders in other sizes, including 5.5kg, 12.5kg, 15kg, 16kg, 18kg, 20kg, 22kg, 25kg, 30kg, 33kg, 35kg and 45kg.

Meanwhile, BERC has set the consumer-level price of autogas at Tk84.62 per litre for October. For LPG supplied through a reticulated system in liquid form, the consumer price has been fixed at Tk149.31 per kg, including VAT.

For gas supplied through a reticulated system, the rate has been set at Tk331.90 per cubic metre. The price of government-supplied LPG at dealer and retailer points remains unchanged at Tk776.93 for a 12.5kg cylinder.

The sharp upward adjustment comes at a time when consumers are already paying significantly higher prices than the regulator-fixed rate amid complaints of supply shortages and higher international costs.

Despite BERC fixing the price of a 12kg cylinder at Tk1,585 for September, consumers have been paying Tk2,000âTk2,500, according to traders and consumers.

The latest price increase is also unlikely to immediately resolve the gap between the regulated and retail prices, particularly if supply constraints persist in some parts of the country, sector insiders said.

The LPG Operators Association of Bangladesh (LOAB), however, has said there is no shortage of LPG in the country and that imports are sufficient to meet domestic demand.

The association recently directed its member companies, distributors, dealers and retailers to sell LPG at prices fixed by BERC.

It said Bangladesh imported around 156,000 tonnes of LPG in September, compared with about 158,000 tonnes in August.

# Bangladeshâs consumers still pay inflated LPG prices as cylinders remain scarce

Author: bdnews24.com News Service

Bangladeshâs consumers still pay inflated LPG prices as cylinders remain scarce

## Importers insist stocks are sufficient, while distributors blame shrinking commissions, rising transport costs and uneven deliveries

 

 bdnews24.com News Service 

 Published : 12 Oct 2026, 01:26 AM 

 Updated : 12 Oct 2026, 01:26 AM 

The price has risen, but the shortage persists. 

Across Dhaka, consumers searching for liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) cylinders are still being quoted prices far above the official rate, while some familiar brands have vanished from shops and unlikely retailers have started selling gas alongside mobile phone top-ups and cement.

On Oct 4, the Bangladesh Energy Regulatory Commission (BERC) raised the price of a 12kg cylinder by Tk 252 to Tk 1,837 for October, up from Tk 1,585. 

Yet consumers continue to pay inflated prices, raising a question: if the price has been adjusted, why has supply not returned to normal?

 

On Wednesday, a resident of Paikpara in Mirpur said a retailer demanded Tk 2,400 for a cylinder, claiming his purchase cost was Tk 2,300.

The LPG Operators Association of Bangladesh (LOAB) says imports are sufficient. 

The country imported 156,000 tonnes in September, close to Augustâs 158,000 tonnes, which the association considers enough to meet demand. 

It has urged the government to act against sellers charging above the official rate.

A Shortage That Outlasted Price Hike

The squeeze began after a fire at a floating liquefied natural gas terminal in Coxâs Bazarâs Moheshkhali on Jul 21 reduced supplies to the national grid. 

LNG supplies returned to normal around mid-September, but LPG prices had already begun climbing, leaving cylinder users paying more even as the piped-gas situation improved.

On Sept 20, the government also raised fuel prices by Tk 20 per litre. LPG businesses subsequently pressed for a cylinder price increase, which BERC announced on Sunday. 

 

The adjustment, however, has not restored normal availability.

âCylinders are expensive to buy. We pay the companyâs dealer in advance. Even then, they donât give us the cylinders,â Noor Hossain Bappi, owner of Bappi Enterprise in Swamibagh, told bdnews24.com.

A visit to shops across Dhaka found cylinders from two of six companies missing from most outlets. Distributors said those companies had stopped supplying cylinders for several weeks and were no longer accepting orders.

Bangladesh has about 10 million LPG customers, around 80 percent of whom use the fuel for household cooking.

 

Importers and Distributors Disagree

Abu Taher Quraishi, treasurer of the LP Gas Business Cooperative Association, said distributors had paid in advance for cylinders due on Monday, Oct 5, the day after the price adjustment.

Companies then demanded the new rate not only for subsequent deliveries but also for cylinders supplied from the beginning of the month.
